pull.title: compressor: oversized script decoding can leave a spendable script
pull.body:
**Problem:** The oversized-script fallback appends `OP_RETURN` to the destination instead of replacing it. If the destination already contains an unfinished push, the appended byte becomes pushed data and the result can remain spendable.

**Fix:** Replace the destination with `OP_RETURN` rather than appending it.

Found while reviewing #36280. This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

> it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.

Not sure, reusing a destination would be an unrelated bug? So I am half suggesting to drop the test in a third commit again, or at least clarify in the comment that this isn't supposed to test any real production behavior.

lgtm either way.

> Not sure, reusing a destination would be an unrelated bug?

We do have some existing reuses, e.g. in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/e7aef7e86da79000aa42f5ba6d13b0d123d9da7c/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L3435-L3462 the snapshot export reuses the same `Coin` in the loop. Regardless, added a comment clarifying that this tests the fallback directly, since normal UTXO insertion excludes oversized scripts.

Tested ACK f313faff443e5cdbd858a54c6bb939799d7ce714

I built test_bitcoin (GCC 13.3, RelWithDebInfo) and ran compress_tests on this and on 11494efb01d0. Both are clean. Putting `script << OP_RETURN` back makes compress_oversized_script fail, so the new check covers the fix.

test: characterize oversized script decoding into a reused target

Decode an oversized script into a target containing an incomplete push.
Record that the resulting script fails IsUnspendable().
The following fix requires the decoded script to be unspendable.

compressor: replace oversized scripts instead of appending

The oversized-script fallback appends OP_RETURN to the destination rather than replacing it as documented.
A reused target retains its previous contents, and an incomplete push can consume OP_RETURN as data.
Assign a new OP_RETURN script before skipping the oversized payload so the result is independent of the destination's prior contents.
